Turbine engines don't fail without warning — the warning is buried in 21 sensor channels most maintenance schedules never read closely. This model reads them, learns the shape of degradation from NASA's C-MAPSS benchmark, and outputs a single number: cycles remaining before failure.

Sensor Trend

Degradation, Caught Early

The Pipeline

From Raw Sensors To A Cycle Count

01

LSTM Reads The Trend

Processes rolling sensor windows, learning how degradation evolves over time. RMSE: 14.47 cycles.

02

XGBoost As Baseline

Same task, tree-based model — RMSE ~18 cycles. Used to validate the LSTM earns its complexity.

03

RUL, In Cycles

Output is a single number — cycles remaining before failure — with a known error margin.

Under The Hood

Industry-Standard Benchmark

Built on NASA's C-MAPSS turbofan degradation dataset — the same benchmark used across predictive maintenance research.

PyTorch LSTM XGBoost Pandas / NumPy Scikit-learn Streamlit

RUL Estimator predicts Remaining Useful Life for turbofan engines using sensor telemetry, trained and validated on NASA's C-MAPSS degradation benchmark.
